title: Over the Top
hook: You can't see the other side of the hill.
scene: The road climbs to a crest and drops away, and beyond it a curve you can't see the far end of. Whatever is on the other side is already coming toward you.

source.psdp_skill: Skill twelve: driving on rural roads
source.teaching_target: PSDP twelve Hills and curves + DOL 5.6 (Curves). Blind crest then curve.

image_brief.subject: the gravel/asphalt climbs to a crest and drops away into a curve whose far end you cannot see
image_brief.foreground: worn black wheel, faded pink dash, coarse mesh; closed dark carrier latched and strapped on the passenger floor (Gracie inside; wheels turning)
image_brief.midground: road rising to a blind crest; beyond the top only sky and the start of a curve
image_brief.background: overcast rural ridge, fir edges, no oncoming grille yet visible
image_brief.read: you cannot see the other side of the hill; a curve begins beyond the crest
extra_negatives: no clear view past the crest
no second person in the car
no cat loose on the seat
no "ginger tabby" wording — use orange tabby markings behind the grille
no carrier door facing outboard toward camera
no empty carrier with no cat visible behind grille
no belt not routed through handle
no low dash-level mesh band only
no brightly lit dash by default
no speedlike 112 LCD readout (odo/trip numerals OK if not live speed)

geometry.ego_lane_side: right half of a two-lane rural road climbing to a crest
geometry.ego_nose_in_frame: plow points up-frame at the blind crest

image_brief.standing_carrier_spec: hard-sided; wire grille door facing inboard; Gracie's orange tabby markings visible behind the grille; belt routed through the handle
image_brief.standing_biome: Cascades-west PNW wet backcountry — restricted sightlines, second-growth fir crowding the shoulder, blackberry and alder in the ditch, vegetation close to the road, wet gray asphalt; NOT sage, dry grass, bare hills, or long open highway

variation.forced: Act VI wave-1 briefs landed; stills pending review; do not seed

decision: Blind crest, then a curve. How do you take it?

options.text: Slow before the crest, move right, look as far through as you can
options.result: You come off it early, hold right, and the far side turns out to have a tractor in the middle of the road with the sun behind it.

options.text: Keep your speed — you'll see it when you're over
options.result: Over the top at speed with a tractor at forty yards and nothing but reflex left.

options.text: Move left for a better view around the curve
options.result: You improve your sightline by putting the Menace in the oncoming lane on a blind hill.

options.text: Brake in the middle of the curve once you can see
options.result: Braking mid-bend on gravel is how the back end goes around. The curve owns the car now.

debrief: Slow down before a crest or a curve, move to the right, and watch for what's coming.
